How much does it cost to carpet a home in Mukilteo, WA?

Plan on $4–$7 per square foot installed once carpet, pad, labor, tack strip and haul-away are added up. Most Mukilteo projects land in the $2,400–$3,900 range, and a single bedroom often comes in around $600–$1,000. The carpet grade you choose moves the total more than anything else — and you choose it with the samples lying on your own floor, not under store lighting.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come out to Mukilteo?

It does. The van carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades to any Mukilteo address, from the Old Town flats up through the Harbour Pointe hills. Samples go on the exact floor being replaced so the color reads true in your light; then we measure every room and staircase and leave a written price before we go. The visit costs nothing.
What do you charge to stretch carpet in Mukilteo?

Stretching starts at $99 per room, and most Mukilteo rooms land between $99–$180 depending on size and how much furniture is in play. A power stretch takes out wrinkles, ridges and trip hazards for roughly a fifth of what new carpet would cost, which makes it the smart move whenever the carpet itself is still in good shape.
What does it cost to carpet the stairs in a Mukilteo two-story?

Stair carpet starts at $18 per step, in either a waterfall wrap or a tailored cap-and-band finish. Mukilteo's sloped-lot floor plans tend to add landings and pie-shaped turns, and every one of them is counted in the written quote at the measure — none of it appears later as a surprise charge.
How long will my Mukilteo carpet installation take?

One day covers most Mukilteo homes. Three or four bedrooms plus a staircase is a normal day for the crew; a whole house with heavy furniture or more than one stairway can carry into a second day. Your quote spells out the schedule in writing, so you know before install day rather than during it.
Will the installers move my furniture, or is that on me?

The crew does the heavy lifting on most jobs — beds, dressers, couches and tables get moved out of the way and set back where they belong. We ask you to handle the small things ahead of time: closet floors, cords and electronics, breakables, and anything personal you'd rather box up yourself.
Is my carpet worth restretching, or should I replace it?

Restretch when the pile still stands up, the backing is sound and you still like the color — that's a $99-per-room fix instead of a full re-carpet. Replace when traffic lanes are matted flat, seams are pulling open, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor returns after professional cleaning. We look first and tell you straight which job yours is.

All of them — Old Town by the ferry dock, Harbour Pointe, Chennault Beach, Olympus Terrace and everything along the Speedway in between. The van also runs to Everett, Edmonds, Lynnwood, Mill Creek and the rest of south Snohomish County, and it rides the ferry to Whidbey Island when a job calls for it.
What carpet stands up best to dogs and cats?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, laid over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents from ever reaching the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber keeps its color even when cleaned with diluted bleach. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot, and it rides in the van so you can feel it before choosing.
Is the installation itself covered by a warranty?

Yes — every install carries a 1-year workmanship warranty from OC Flooring, on top of the mill's wear-and-stain warranty on the carpet itself, typically 10 to 25 years depending on grade. Both go on your written quote. Worth knowing: some mills tie their coverage to the pad underneath, which is exactly why all three pad grades come along on the visit.
